processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: The material was melted in a high-vacuum electric-arc melting furnace.
Ingots were hot rolled from 20 to 2 mm at 1000 °C (hot-rolled state is the prehistory of the M2-SS sample).
Hot-rolled ingots followed by water quenching.
Samples were solution-processed at 1000 °C for 30 min and water quenched; the two solution-treated steels were named M1-SS and M2-SS.

structures.overall_structure: Equiaxed austenite grains (single-phase austenite matrix) containing intragranular (Ti,V)C carbides; no significant texture; bimodal grain size distribution

grain_structure.grain_size_distribution: bimodal (small grains embedded around larger ones)

precipitates.distribution: intragranular, dispersed within the grain interior; particle density higher than in M1

measurement_conditions.specimen_geometry: tensile specimens 2 mm thick, 58 mm long, fabricated along the rolling direction; 12.5 mm extensometer
measurement_conditions.other_conditions: Yield strength determined at a 0.2 % offset

tensile_properties.stress_strain_curves: Engineering stress–engineering strain curve (Fig. 7a) and true stress–true strain / strain-hardening rate curves (Fig. 7b) for M2-SS (red dotted curve in the four-curve legend)
tensile_properties.strain_hardening_rate: M2-SS strain-hardening index curve almost coincides with M2-30 (Fig. 11b), indicating preserved work-hardening ability

characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: 200 × magnification; etched with 3 % FeCl3 + 10 % HCl (in ethanol) for 10–20 s; grain size per GB/T 6394-2002
characterization_methods.purpose: Characterize phase morphology and grain structure of M2-SS (Fig. 1c)
characterization_methods.key_findings: M2-SS shows finer equiaxed grains and a dense dispersion of fine dark particles compared with M1-SS

characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: Observation plane consistent with metallographic examination surface; electrochemical polishing for strain-free surfaces; 50 µm scale bar
characterization_methods.purpose: Determine texture and grain-size distribution of M2-SS (Fig. 2a)
characterization_methods.key_findings: Random colour distribution indicating absence of significant texture; bimodal grain-size distribution with small grains embedded around larger ones

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: TEM, Thermo Fisher Scientific, Talos F200X G2; BF/DF imaging and SAED
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: Samples ground to 50 μm, 3 mm discs, thinned with Gatan precision ion polishing system; 1 µm scale bar
characterization_methods.purpose: Characterize the intragranular precipitates in M2-SS (Fig. 3b)
characterization_methods.key_findings: Numerous fine dark dot-like intragranular precipitates identified as (Ti,V)C carbides; intragranular (Ti,V)C average size 35.8 ± 20.1 nm; M1-SS matrix shows no precipitates

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: Electronic universal testing machine, SUNS, UTM5105X; 12.5 mm extensometer
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: Room temperature; strain rate 10^-3 s^-1; yield strength at 0.2 % offset
characterization_methods.purpose: Measure mechanical properties (yield strength, tensile curves) of M2-SS
characterization_methods.key_findings: Solution-treated M2 steel exhibited ~200 MPa higher yield strength than M1-SS due to (Ti,V)C precipitation

computational_details.simulation_method: Olson–Cohen thermodynamic model for stacking-fault energy (SFE)
computational_details.boundary_and_initial_conditions: At a certain temperature the SFE influencing factors relate only to the composition
computational_details.validation_against_experiment: Calculated SFE indicates dislocation slip deformation mode, consistent with TEM observation of planar/dislocation slip in M2

analytical_models.equation_role: Compute stacking-fault energy from composition and grain-size effect

parameters.name: ρ (molar surface density on {111} planes) for M2

analytical_models.model_note: Ti and V elements have little influence on the SFE; excess part ΔG_ex ≈ 1–2 mJ/m^2 is approximately the same for M1 and M2

computational_details.validation_against_experiment: Confirms the matrix remains single-phase austenite after aging treatment

unmapped_findings: For M2-SS, no κ-carbides are quantified (Table 3 shows a dash for κ in M2-SS); only (Ti,V)C carbides are present (2.4 ± 1.4 %, mean radius 35.8 ± 20.1 nm).

The addition of Ti and V does not alter the austenitic phase composition of the low-density steel but refines the grain size; the M2-SS grain size is 32.3 ± 10.4 μm versus 42.4 ± 7.8 μm for the Ti/V-free M1-SS.

(Ti,V)C carbides are high-temperature precipitates (precipitation temperatures of Ti and V exceed 1000 °C) that form before aging and remain stable, so their size and volume fraction do not change under aging.
The calculated SFE of M2 (≈78 mJ/m²) indicates the deformation mode of the material is dislocation slip, consistent with TEM observations of planar slip.

Fig. 10 (strengthening mechanism bar chart) indicates M2-SS measured yield strength lies between 600 and 800 MPa, with calculated contributions σ0 + σG + σOr (no κ shear strengthening σS); however no numeric labels are printed on the chart.

The two solution-treated steels (M1-SS and M2-SS) were produced by the same process (proc_ss-1000c-30min) but differ in composition; M2-SS exhibits ~200 MPa higher yield strength than M1-SS due to (Ti,V)C precipitation.
